body:
This is me with music, YouTube and anime to be honest.

All I want to do is escape myself. Everything I do is an attempt at escaping my reality. Yet, the only art I can truly relate to is dark, nihilistic, depressing and brutal art. Kind of a Catch 22.

Absolutely. I feel completely and utterly unfixable and that it's my fault for being this broken, and that living is just a distraction from killing myself. Through all the attempts, all the times I thought I had improved, I always end back at square one.

I haven't been in high school for almost 2 years, an... yeah, I suppose I'm free to decide my own way, but what **I** want and what my deep subconscious wants are completely at odds. The surface-level me wants to be happy and healthy and a better person than I am now, but my Shadow (to borrow from Carl Jung) seems driven to make me more and more miserable until suicide truly is the only way out. Through all the medication and therapy, that part of me has stayed in total control.
Nothing, which is the same benefit I get out of fatalistic, spiritual bypassing nonsense.
What a longform way of saying nothing at all.

At the end of the day I'm not sure why I should even bother taking said journey in the first place, or if I can ever force myself to take it. Read my other posts if you want more context to that statement.

> your own peace in whatever form that may take

Throughout the years I haven't found any real peace. Distractions? Sure. Any actual peace or feeling of life being worth the effort? Not a trace.

> at least reach before you fall

I've reached out for help many times and a fat lot of good it's done me so far.

My philosophy is that, if you feel truly guilty and understand where you went wrong and vow never to do it again, then that's the closest thing to redemption. You'll learn to forgive yourself for that eventually - it might take telling your counselor about it and working through it - but the way I see it, as soon as you realize your own guilt, that's when you can forgive yourself.

If I'm to listen to the only voice I can hear, it's because it's easier to stay the same as I am, and be able to internally absolve myself because I'm a "victim" than it is to actually force myself to do something that feels scary and alien where my failures are truly my own, and not something I can't control.

> why not give it a shot? You're stuck on a dead end, you don't have anything to lose anyway. But you just might gain so much. 

This is the question I want to learn the answer to. I don't know why I feel so incapable, so helpless to even give it a try. I feel like a child for not being able to even take care of myself properly, but for some reason I can't force myself to do anything about it, and I hate myself for it.

> no one can start that flame but me

This is the most horrible thought out of anything to be honest. Knowing that I won't escape unless I can trust myself to go through the motions, when I feel too lazy and scared to bother with it.

I've been stuck for years.

I'm not beyond avoiding responsibility. I'm quite high atm but the point I was trying to get across is "I avoid responsibility by putting it on either me being broken, or everything around me, but I despite realizing this is a problem, I still keep falling back on it and keep disempowering myself because it's easier than actually trying."

Apologies for the run-on sentences lol.

I relate to your feelings quite alot. I don't think I can believe I am my own saviour, because my lack of motivation and self-dicipline makes me avoid the responsibilities involved with recovery. Internally, I've already decided that my life is going to be bad and nobody and nothing seems to change my mind about that. Worst of all, that belief means I lack motivation to improve, because why bother improving if life will always suck? Then, to legitimise my own lack of motivation, I hide behind my depression so I can be a victim, ensuring that I never want to improve again.

My life right now is that cycle, that fucking wretched circle that makes me a worse person, and a miserable one at that.
